questions.question: Explain why phenylamine is a weaker base than ammonia.
questions.answer: The N lone pair in phenylamine is delocalised into the benzene ring, so it is less available to accept H+ than the localised lone pair in NH3.
steps: The N lone pair of phenylamine overlaps with the pi system of the benzene ring.
This delocalisation spreads the electron density, so the lone pair is held less tightly on N.
Less electron density is available on N to accept a proton.
NH3 has a localised lone pair, so it is the stronger base.

questions.question: Explain why the ionic radius of Tm3+ (0.095 nm) is less than that of Ce3+ (0.111 nm).
questions.answer: Tm has more protons, so greater nuclear charge pulls the electrons in more strongly; 4f electrons shield poorly, giving the lanthanide contraction.
steps: Across the lanthanides the nuclear charge increases by one proton per element.
Added 4f electrons shield each other poorly.
The effective nuclear charge on the outer electrons increases, so the ion shrinks.
Tm3+ therefore has a smaller radius than Ce3+.

questions.question: Suggest why lanthanide complex ions can contain more ligands than transition metal complex ions.
questions.answer: Lanthanide ions are large and their 4f orbitals do not take part in bonding, so bonding is largely electrostatic and non-directional, allowing higher coordination numbers.
steps: Lanthanide ions have large radii, leaving room for more ligands around them.
The 4f orbitals are buried and do not form strong directional bonds.
So bonding is mainly electrostatic, and more ligands can pack around the ion.

questions.question: Hydrated cerium(IV) ammonium nitrate contains 23.97% Ce, 19.18% N, 2.05% H and 54.80% O by mass. Calculate the empirical formula and hence the overall formula showing Ce4+, NH4+, NO3- and water.

In 3-methylhexan-3-ol, C3 carries OH, CH3, ethyl and propyl, all different, so it is chiral.

questions.question: Describe a chemical test, with the result, that could distinguish the Dewar structure from benzene.
questions.answer: Add bromine water: the Dewar structure (which has C=C bonds) decolourises it, whereas benzene does not.
steps: Dewar benzene contains two C=C double bonds.

questions.question: State one similarity and one difference in the low-resolution proton NMR spectra of the Ladenburg structure and benzene, using Data Booklet data.
questions.answer: Similarity: both show one peak because all six H are equivalent. Difference: Ladenburg H are on saturated carbons, appearing at about 0.5-2 ppm rather than the aromatic 6-9 ppm of benzene.
steps: In the Ladenburg structure all six C-H environments are equivalent, as in benzene, so there is one peak in each case.
Benzene's H are on sp2 carbons in an aromatic ring: 6.0-9.0 ppm in the Data Booklet.
Ladenburg H are on sp3 carbons, so they appear at lower shift, around 0.5-2 ppm.
So the peak appears at a different chemical shift.

questions.question: Explain how X-ray diffraction shows that benzene has a delocalised structure rather than a Kekule structure.
questions.answer: X-ray diffraction shows all six C-C bond lengths are equal (about 0.139 nm), intermediate between C-C and C=C, so there are no alternating single and double bonds.
steps: X-ray diffraction measures the positions of electron density and gives bond lengths.
All C-C bonds in benzene are the same length.
This length lies between a C-C single bond (0.154 nm) and a C=C double bond (0.134 nm).
A Kekule structure would show alternating long and short bonds, which is not observed.

questions.topic: Enthalpy Level Diagram for Benzene Isomers
questions.question: Draw a labelled enthalpy level diagram showing the relative stability of the Ladenburg structure, the Dewar structure and benzene, with values -376 and -297 kJ mol-1 for isomerisation to benzene.
questions.answer: Benzene lowest; Dewar about 297 kJ mol-1 above benzene; Ladenburg about 376 kJ mol-1 above benzene.
steps: Isomerisation to benzene is exothermic, so benzene is at the lowest level.
Dewar isomerises with -297 kJ mol-1, so Dewar lies 297 kJ mol-1 above benzene.
Ladenburg isomerises with -376 kJ mol-1, so it lies 376 kJ mol-1 above benzene.
Label each level with its value; Ladenburg is least stable.

questions.question: Give a possible reason why the isomerisation of Dewar benzene to benzene has a lower activation energy than that of the Ladenburg structure.
questions.answer: Dewar benzene is higher in energy and more strained, so less energy is needed to reach the transition state for rearrangement.
steps: Dewar benzene has strained bonds and is less stable than benzene.
Its starting energy is higher, so the energy barrier to rearrangement is lower.
Ladenburg is more strained still, but the barrier to its conversion is higher in this comparison.

questions.question: Devise a reaction scheme (no more than four steps) to prepare propan-1-ol from butanone, giving reagents, essential conditions and intermediates.
questions.answer: (1) I2 and NaOH, warm (iodoform reaction) gives sodium propanoate; (2) dilute HCl gives propanoic acid; (3) LiAlH4 in dry ether, then water, gives propan-1-ol.
steps: Butanone is a methyl ketone, so the iodoform reaction removes the CH3CO group as CHI3 (yellow precipitate).
Step 1: I2 with NaOH(aq), warm, gives sodium propanoate, CH3CH2COO- Na+, plus CHI3.
Step 2: acidify with dilute HCl to give propanoic acid, CH3CH2COOH.
Step 3: reduce with LiAlH4 in dry ether, then add water, to give propan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2OH.

questions.question: Devise a reaction scheme (no more than four steps) to prepare 2-methylbut-2-ene from butanone, giving reagents, conditions and intermediates.
questions.answer: (1) CH3MgBr in dry ether, then dilute acid, gives 2-methylbutan-2-ol; (2) hot concentrated H2SO4 or H3PO4 (dehydration) gives 2-methylbut-2-ene.
steps: Step 1: CH3MgBr (Grignard) adds to the C=O of butanone in dry ether, forming an alkoxide.
Hydrolysis with dilute acid gives the tertiary alcohol 2-methylbutan-2-ol, (CH3)2C(OH)CH2CH3.
Step 2: heat with concentrated H2SO4 or H3PO4 (acid-catalysed elimination), losing water.
Major product 2-methylbut-2-ene (Saytzeff product); 2-methylbut-1-ene is a minor product.
Distil off the alkene as it forms to shift the equilibrium.

steps: The two CH3 groups are equivalent: one doublet from coupling to the CH proton.
The CH proton couples to six CH3 protons, giving a heptet.
The OH proton does not split and appears as a singlet.

questions.question: A substituted benzene has general formula CnH2n-6. 0.025 mol produced 11.0 g CO2 on complete combustion. Which could be its Mr? A 64, B 78, C 128, D 134.
steps: Carbon per molecule = 0.250/0.025 = 10, so n = 10.
